You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
node.criteria: Return complete if s1 passes. Otherwise, return absent only if s1 fails and s2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial if s1 fails and s2 passes, establishing incomplete progress toward the court background. Return unknown if evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved, including when s1 is unknown and completion cannot be established. A pass on s2 does not establish completion, and unrelated edits do not count.
node.binding: Target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.. Reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1..

node_traces.evidence: s1 fails to establish a recognizable basketball-court background, while s2 passes and establishes visible progress toward the requested change. The criteria therefore indicate incomplete progress.

dependencies.evidence: The kitchen background has been replaced with a basketball hoop and balls, but the surrounding scene is a dark, featureless backdrop rather than a recognizable basketball court. No clear court surface or markings are visible as part of the background.

The edited image replaces the kitchen background with visible basketball-related scene elements, including a hoop, basketballs, and court markings, showing clear progress toward the requested background change.

Refine the binding and s1 evidence standard to assess the whole background and accept these visible court features together, rather than treating the dark upper backdrop alone as decisive. Keep s2 as evidence of progress, not completion by itself, and retain the distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unresolved. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport or schema failure; the disagreement is visual/criterion interpretation, not a reason to force the reference label."}
